sentences.text: Campodus is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish belonging to the order Eugeneodontiformes from the Carboniferous.
This animal possessed broad, ridge-ornamented crushing teeth made of various dentine types.
The type species Campodus agassizianus was first described in 1844 from teeth found in the Namurian stage of Belgium.
The genus Campodus was established by Koninck in 1844.
Multiple species have been assigned to Campodus, including C. agassizianus, C. arizonensis, C. basalis, C. corrugatus, C. scitulus, C. variabilis, and C. virginianus.
Campodus lived between the Gzhelian and Roadian stages, approximately 303.7 to 266.9 million years ago.
There is a debate over whether Agassizodus and Campodus are synonyms, as some authors suggest they are the same while others note a lack of overlapping fossil locations.
